evidence: src/infrastructure/inMemoryRepositories.ts: InMemoryUserRepository, InMemoryProjectRepository and InMemoryTaskRepository implement the domain ports UserRepository, ProjectRepository and TaskRepository.

src/infrastructure/app.ts: createApp calls only TaskManagementService methods (createUser, createProject, listProjects, createTask, listTasks, assignTask, markDone) and never calls repositories directly.

src/infrastructure/app.ts: status is validated through the domain's isTaskStatus in both the POST /projects/:projectId/tasks and GET /projects/:projectId/tasks handlers, so the rule is not re-implemented. Only the error message string is repeated.
src/infrastructure/app.ts: a single error middleware maps DomainError.code (validation, not_found, other) to HTTP status codes.
src/infrastructure/server.ts: a minimal entry point that only calls createApp().listen(port).
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The module passes the rule. It is the infrastructure adapter layer for a task API. app.ts is the HTTP adapter, inMemoryRepositories.ts is the persistence adapter and server.ts is the entry point. Together they form one concern: the concrete outer ring that wires the application service to the outside world.

The module uses its own abstractions consistently. The repositories implement the domain ports. app.ts reaches all behaviour through TaskManagementService and never touches repositories or entities directly. Status validation goes through the domain's isTaskStatus helper instead of re-implementing the set of allowed values. Error mapping is centralised in a single Express error handler keyed on DomainError.code.

There are two small repetitions in app.ts, neither of which duplicates a business rule:
- The message string "status must be todo, in_progress or done" is written out twice.
- The "assigneeId must be a string" check is done inline in the query handler instead of through the str() helper.

The validation rule itself still lives in one place (isTaskStatus), so these are cosmetic. Having createApp default to in-memory repositories makes app.ts a small composition root, which is normal for this layer.
